Your eleven projects 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He sits 0.3 clear of Salah and carries meaningful upside: a 25% chance of 10 or more, against an 8% tail risk of 2 or fewer. The captaincy is tight enough that Salah remains a live alternative, but the model sees Haaland as the marginally stronger play.

You are three-deep in both Arsenal and Manchester City. That concentration is backed by their projections—Raya, Gabriel and Saka all feature among your eleven's stronger scores, and Haaland is your captain—but it does mean your ceiling and floor move together if either club underperforms.

No transfer clears the points it would cost. You have one free move and £0.5m in the bank. Mykolenko on the bench at 3.1 is the best available swap-in, but nothing in the eleven projects closely enough to him to make a single-move upgrade viable.

Hold and play.

Your eleven projects 69.0 with Haaland captained. He is 0.3 clear of Salah and carries real upside — a quarter chance of double digits against a 8% tail of 2 or fewer — so the armband choice is sound.

You hold your free transfer. No swap improved the total enough to justify its cost, which is the right discipline at this stage.

You have three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That concentration in three clubs is worth monitoring, but it reflects their current standing rather than a flaw in the squad.

Your bench projects 10.7, led by Mykolenko at 3.1. The depth is thin if injuries strike, but it is a week-to-week trade-off you are managing consciously. Come next week, revisit whether the free transfer sitting unused can strengthen either your starting eleven or your cover.

Your team projects 69.0 points with Haaland armband. He is a narrow favourite—only 0.3 clear of Salah—but no alternative came out ahead once transfer costs were accounted for, so you are holding your free transfer.

You have three Arsenal players in the eleven and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That concentration reflects their projections rather than any attempt at balance, but it does mean you are heavily reliant on those three clubs this week.

The bench offers little cover. Mykolenko at 3.1 is the only substitute worth mentioning, and only barely. If anyone in your starting eleven fails to play, you will be short.

Nothing in the numbers suggests a move, but the tightness of the captain race—Haaland's edge is thin—means this week carries more variance than the projection alone suggests.
